chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Ismāʿīl al-Juʿfī, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Regarding blood that is on a garment: if it is less than the measure of a dirham, then he does not repeat the salat (prayer). But if it is more than the measure of a dirham, and he had seen it but did not wash it until he prayed, then let him repeat his salat (prayer). And if he had not seen it until he prayed, then he does not repeat the salat (prayer).

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment or clothing worn in prayer
key_terms.رَآهُ: he saw it, meaning he was aware of the impurity
key_terms.فَلَمْ يَغْسِلْهُ: he did not wash it before praying
key_terms.قَدْرِ دِرْهَمٍ: the measure of a dirham used as the legal threshold

ai.seo_question: Does one have to repeat salat (prayer) if there was blood on the clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about blood on a garment during salat (prayer). It distinguishes between a small amount and a larger amount, and also between deliberate neglect after seeing the blood and ignorance of it until after the prayer.
